long_description:

Ready to make something special? Book your place today and create a pair of unique, handmade earrings just in time for the festive season!

id: Timeline - 300 Years of Music for Saxophone-St Michael's Anglican Church, 81 Upland Rd, Kelburn, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Timeline - 300 Years of Music for Saxophone
venue: St Michael's Anglican Church, 81 Upland Rd, Kelburn, Wellington
long_description:
Join us as we explore the history of the saxophone through 300 years of music performed by an exciting yet subtle chamber duo.

This concert explores a broad range of music, from pieces by J.S Bach which predate the saxophone by over 100 years, to modern compositions which push the limits of the instrument. Between these moments you will hear some of the greatest works for saxophone, from the popular showcase Pequeña Czarda to the elegant staple Tableaux de Provence.

Hear the many moods and timbres of the saxophone, from delicately soaring melodies, to dark, enchanting arias and joyful, raucous moments.

Programme:
J.S. Bach - Partita No. 2 for Solo Violin: IV. Gigue
Robert Schumann - 3 Romances
J. B Singelée - Concertino Op. 78
Eugène Bozza - Aria
Pierre Lantier - Sicilienne
Pedro Itturalde - Pequeña Czarda
Paul Bonneau - Caprice en Forme de Valse
Paule Maurice - Tableaux de Provence
Steven Banks - Surrender

$25 pre-sale
$35 door sales
$10 student/concession

About the performers:
Alex Trask is a saxophonist based in Pōneke. He has a keen interest in the classical saxophone and has studied with some of New Zealand's leading player such as Simon Brew and Reuben Chin. He is a member of the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and has performed with many other significant organizations such as Gallery Orchestra, Saxcess, Wellington Youth Orchestra, and Wellington City Symphonic Band.

Alex is also an accomplished jazz player, and has performed all over the country. In 2026 he appeared with the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, as well as playing lead alto for the RNZAF Jazz Orchestra. Alex helf the lead alto chair in the Rodger Fox Big Band from 2024-2025 and has performed as a guest with that band since 2022. In 2026 he recorded his first studio album, which will be released in 2027.

Gabriela Glapska is a Polish-born, Wellington-based pianist celebrated for her expressive artistry, versatility, and collaborative spirit. An accomplished soloist, chamber musician, and sought-after accompanist, she brings clarity, depth, and nuance to a wide range of musical settings.
 
Gabriela holds a Master’s degree with Distinction from the Feliks Nowowiejski Academy of Music in Bydgoszcz, where she studied under renowned pianist Ewa Pobłocka, and a PhD in Music Performance from Victoria University of Wellington. She currently works as a collaborative pianist at Te Kōkī – New Zealand School of Music.

Whether performing in concert halls, schools, or contemporary music spaces, Gabriela Glapska is known for her refined musicianship, intuitive ensemble playing, and passionate advocacy for music in all its forms.

long_description:
In Search of My Moehau (2026)

Directors: Kieran Charnock and Jonathan Watt
Genre: Drama / Comedy | Rated M
Venue: Circus Cinema, Martinborough
Date: Saturday 7 November 2026 | 3pm

Tickets: Book directly through Circus Cinema. Make a phone reservation: 06 306 9442 or book online: https://www.circus.net.nz/films

About the film

What begins as a search for a missing father takes a decidedly strange turn in In Search of My Moehau, a darkly comic found-footage mockumentary set deep in the New Zealand bush.

Morris Fubbins is convinced his father has been taken by a mythical creature. As his search unfolds, folklore, obsession and the absurd collide in this offbeat New Zealand feature, bringing a distinctly Kiwi twist to the found-footage tradition popularised by The Blair Witch Project.

Meet the filmmaker

We're delighted to welcome director Jonathan Watt to the screening. Jonathan will introduce the film and stay afterwards to answer questions, offering audiences an opportunity to hear more about the making of the film and the creative thinking behind this wonderfully unconventional story.

A special Spring Sessions screening

Hot off the festival circuit, In Search of My Moehau enjoyed a successful run at Whānau Mārama New Zealand International Film Festival, screening in Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Masterton.

We're pleased to bring the film to Circus Cinema, Martinborough, as part of Te Waiwhakaata Wairarapa Film Festival's Spring Sessions 2026. Directors Kieran Charnock and Jonathan Watt have strong Wairarapa connections and have been making films together for more than 20 years.

This is a special opportunity to experience the film on the big screen and meet one of the filmmakers.

Saturday 7 November | 3pm
Circus Cinema, Martinborough

See the films, meet the filmmaker.

Friday 20 November 2026 | 7:30pm

Director: Joel Coen | Country: USA | Duration: 1h 38m | Genre: Comedy, Crime, Drama, Thriller | Classification: R18

*A lot can happen in the middle of nowhere.*

The Coen brothers’ darkly comic crime classic takes us to the snow-covered landscapes of Minnesota, where a desperate car salesman hatches a seemingly simple plan to solve his financial troubles: have his wife kidnapped and collect the ransom from her wealthy father.

But when the plan goes horribly wrong, a trail of violence leads to the unflappable and very pregnant Police Chief Marge Gunderson, whose quiet determination and sharp instincts bring her ever closer to the truth.

Blending pitch-black humour, suspense and unforgettable characters, *Fargo* is a brilliantly offbeat portrait of ordinary people making extraordinarily bad decisions.

Winner of two Academy Awards, including Best Actress for Frances McDormand, *Fargo* remains one of the Coen brothers’ most celebrated films.

95% on Rotten Tomatoes

Come and experience this modern classic on the big screen as we celebrate its 30th anniversary.

venue: Waikanae Arts and Crafts Society, 27a Elizabeth St, Waikanae
long_description:
Impressions of Nature on Silk

Eco dyeing, also known as leaf or eco print, is a gentle, alchemical process where the natural pigments of leaves are transferred directly onto fabric, creating one-of-a-kind botanical imprints.

Join me for a full day of slow making and discovery as we explore this beautiful dialogue between nature and cloth. In the morning, we’ll forage around the hall, gathering leaves and foliage that speak to us. You’ll learn how to prepare and bundle silk with plant materials, drawing out colours and patterns from the landscape itself.

In the afternoon, you’ll design and dye your own silk scarf — a wearable memory of place and season, marked by the delicate traces of nature’s touch.

You will learn

• which plants and fibres work best for this method
• how to use an iron mordant to enhance colour and detail
• different bundling techniques and approaches

All materials and tools will be provided for use during the workshop.

Your workshop fee includes silk fabrics to explore and experiment with, one silk scarf to design and dye, and a detailed handout with information on mordants, dye plants, tips, and useful resources.

A ‘what to bring’ list (including suggestions for clothing and optional items) will be sent out closer to the workshop date.

long_description:
Celebrated songwriter Kristin Hersh will return to New Zealand this November / December for a run of four main centre intimate headline shows in support of her forthcoming new album Sugar On Blackstone, out 18 September via Fire Records.

Renowned for her fiercely emotional performances and uncompromising songwriting, Hersh’s New Zealand dates will see her bring songs from Sugar On Blackstone to audiences across the country alongside highlights from her extensive catalogue.

Following on from 2023’s Clear Pond Road, Sugar On Blackstone is a darker yet delicately rendered collection exploring life and death, memory, survival and human connection. Deeply personal and emotionally expansive, the album reflects on the lasting bonds between musicians, family and friends, and the way certain sounds and places can suddenly bring someone vividly back into focus.

New single ‘Dark-Eyed Junco’ offers another striking glimpse into the album, pairing lucid melodies with deeply autobiographical storytelling. Recorded at Stable Sound Studios, the album features longtime collaborators Rob Ahlers (50FOOTWAVE) on drums and Pete Harvey (Throwing Muses) on cello.

Long celebrated as one of alternative music’s most singular voices, Hersh continues to deliver performances that are both intensely intimate and disarmingly powerful - a rare opportunity to experience one of modern music’s most influential songwriters up close.

long_description:
Join us for Professor Tristram Ingham's Inaugural Professorial Lecture, titled "Ōritetanga | Equity. One principle. One journey among many." If you'd like to attend, either in person or via the livestream, please register via the link above. This lecture will be followed by light refreshments.

About Professor Tristram Ingham's research:

Tristram (Ngāti Kahungunu ki Heretaunga, Ngāti Porou) is a clinical epidemiologist with decades of experience in healthcare research. His work advances equity across respiratory health, tāngata whaikaha Māori (Māori disability) and health services’ governance. He uses kaupapa Māori and mixed-methods research to translate evidence into policy and system change in Aotearoa.

Tristram led the development of Whāia Te Ao Mārama, the Māori Disability Action Plan 2018-2022 and is Chair of the Te Ao Mārama Aotearoa Trust, a nationwide organisation representing Tāngata Whaikaha Māori. He was made a Companion of the King’s Service Order (KSO) in the 2025 New Year Honours for services to survivors of abuse in care. In 2024, he received the ONZM for services to the disability community.

Tristram is an honorary fellow of the New Zealand College of Public Health Medicine, a member of the Institute of Directors New Zealand and a member of the Royal Society Te Apārangi.

venue: The Circus Cinema, Bar and Cafe, 34 Jellicoe St, Martinborough
long_description:
Barry Barclay Retrospective

Wairarapa (1968) + Barry Barclay: The Camera on the Shore (2009). Presented as part of Te Waiwhakaata Wairarapa Film Festival's Spring Sessions 2026, this special retrospective celebrates the work and legacy of groundbreaking Aotearoa filmmaker Barry Barclay (Ngāti Apa). Bringing together two films connected to Barclay's significant contribution to cinema, this screening offers audiences an opportunity to discover his work and see a newly preserved piece of Wairarapa's film history on the big screen.

Wairarapa (1968)

Camera: Barry Barclay
Promotional film | 22 minutes
Made for the Wairarapa Development Council for distribution throughout the world, Wairarapa is a promotional film showcasing the natural beauty, outdoor activities and rural life of the region. From mountain landscapes and wildlife to farming and local events, the film captures a fascinating portrait of Wairarapa in 1968. Newly preserved by Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision, this screening offers a rare opportunity to experience the film on the big screen and revisit a remarkable piece of our region's cinematic heritage.

Barry Barclay: The Camera on the Shore (2009)
Director: Graeme Tuckett
Documentary | 1 hour 42 minutes
A career-spanning documentary exploring the life and work of groundbreaking Aotearoa filmmaker Barry Barclay. Structured around an interview with Barclay shortly before his death in 2008, the documentary offers an insight into his filmmaking career, creative vision and enduring contribution to Indigenous cinema. Together, these two films provide an opportunity to celebrate Barry Barclay's legacy and reflect on the importance of preserving and sharing Aotearoa's film heritage.

Circus Cinema, Martinborough
Tickets: Book directly through Circus Cinema. Click the Book Tickets link to go to their online booking form, or phone 06 306 9442. Book here: https://www.circus.net.nz/book-film

Now, Come Together is taking that spirit out to the festival fields.

Expect huge songs, exceptional musicianship and plenty of moments guaranteed to have audiences out of their seats and singing at the top of their lungs.

And best of all? It’s the ultimate festival experience without the mud, the rain or the portaloo queues.

Julia Cooper is an Aotearoa singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Best known as the front woman and co-founder of Aotearoa’s well loved band ‘Dr Reknaw’. Julia has recently birthed her solo project ‘Jullekke’. She is recognised for her smooth, velvety & sultry vocal tones, catchy trance bass and guitar riff. Her lyricism features an ethereal quality mixed with messages of empowerment, consciousness and healing. With flavours of roots, soul, world tastes and funk. As a true sonic missionary, Nikau is creating a soothing “golden-era sound” as part of his mission to heal with his music. The songs of Casual Healing emphasise life lessons of aroha, peace and unity through powerful lyrical scribe woven into smooth reggae, soul rhythm. This infusion creates a unique nostalgic vibe, creating a captivating and comforting essence that evokes recollections of moments shared with friends and whānau. Casual Healing's goal is to create songs that “make people feel like they want to be better people”, drawing inspiration from Bob Marley, who showed us the power of compassion and simplicity.

This enchanting songstress radiates strength through vulnerability & the connections awakened from returning to our roots. A blend of Te Reo Māori & English, this powerful set will echo through your bones & reverberate your soul. HINE recently released her debut EP 'KA MUA KA MURI' with a national tour, leading the EP to place #1 on the Aotearoa Official Top Charts. This will be HINE’s last tour of the North Island before a move to Ōtautahi and then travel internationally.

name: Exploring Landscapes in Oil & Cold Wax Painting Workshop
venue: Karen Piercy Art Studio, 98 Paetawa Road, Peka Peka, Waikanae
long_description:
Exploratory Landscapes in Oil & Cold Wax

Discover how to create expressive, atmospheric landscapes using oil paint and cold wax medium in my purpose-built studio, set within a garden setting.

Through layered colour, rich textures and intuitive mark making, you'll explore how to build depth, mood and a sense of place. Learn how suggested rather than literal forms can evoke land, rock and plant life, and how just a few carefully placed marks can transform an abstract surface into a compelling landscape.

The morning will be devoted to a series of practical exercises introducing you to different oil and cold wax techniques. You'll experiment with layering, blending, texture, mark making and ways of suggesting landscape forms. In the afternoon, you'll put these techniques into practice, creating several A4 and A3 paintings on oil paper, exploring your own ideas and developing your personal approach to this versatile medium.

This small, supportive workshop encourages experimentation and discovery in a relaxed, inspiring garden studio environment. Whether you're new to oil and cold wax or looking to extend your existing practice, you'll leave with a collection of original paintings, new skills and plenty of ideas to continue exploring.

What's included:

All painting materials and the use of professional tools

An 8-page take-home handout on oil and cold wax

Tea and coffee throughout the day

Your own paintings to take home

Workshop details

Cost: $195 per person

Group size: Maximum of 4 participants, ensuring individual guidance and support

Venue: Karen Piercy's purpose-built garden studio

What to bring: Please bring your own lunch, an apron or old clothes, and cardboard or a shallow box suitable for transporting your paintings home (up to A3 size). Your work will be interleaved with baking paper for safe transport.

id: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)

Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura Performing Arts Centre, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

This collaboration will be presented in both Kāpiti and Wellington.

Duration: Approximately 2 hours including interval.

long_description:
This holiday season, choose to give and change a life! The Giving Machine is a unique vending machine where, instead of buying snacks, you can purchase goods and services to support those in need. It’s a machine that enables a person to give—rather than receive. Help bring some joy to those in our local Wellington community who could use support.

The Giving Machine is part of the Light the World Initiative—an annual effort from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints inviting everyone to celebrate the birth and life of Jesus Christ by serving others.
